problem: Image-space VLM spatial grounding methods (RoboPoint, RoboRefer) output 2D points tied to visible pixels, so they fail to infer local navigation targets that are occluded by furniture or people, and they often land on non-traversable structure.
motivation: Language-conditioned local navigation in cluttered indoor scenes often requires choosing a feasible target behind occluders (e.g. 'go behind the table'). Ego-centric BEV representations preserve metric ground-plane structure under occlusion, and injecting 3D/BEV cues into VLMs is known to help ego-centric tasks, motivating a BEV affordance output.
key_idea: Predict a dense ego-centric BEV affordance heatmap by fusing an ego-aligned VLM's [NAV] embedding with depth-derived BEV geometry features, trained with geodesic target-region supervision including explicit negatives.
insight: Gains come from the combination of components, not from supervised adaptation alone: a same-VLM + MLP point head reaches only 41.25 GeoAcc vs 57.72 for BEACON. Removing BEV encoder/output raises SIR on the occluded subset from about 2.6 to 11-16.5, so BEV-space modeling drives structural validity. 3D position encoding helps only when combined with Stage-1 ego-centric instruction tuning (alone it drops occluded GeoAcc to 37.93).
method: Ego-Centric 3D Position Encoding: depth-derived agent-frame 3D position of each patch token is passed through a 2-layer MLP and added to the ViT token before the projector (LLaVA-3D/SpatialVLA style, adapted to four surround views).
[NAV] task token: a special token appended to the prompt; its final hidden state is the compact instruction-conditioned embedding for the decoder.
Stage-1 auto-derived instruction tuning: LM loss on templated direction (8 bins) and range (small/big, 2.4 m) answers derived from the annotated target; trains projector, E3D and LoRA.

Geometry-Aware BEV Encoder: BEV-pooled DINOv2 image features plus SECOND-style 3D-conv voxel depth features, mixed with a per-cell gate G predicted from a ray-cast free-space cue M, then 1x1 projected.

Post-Fusion Affordance Decoder: upsamples the [NAV] embedding to the BEV grid, concatenates with F_BEV, and applies a BEVFusion fusion module plus conv layers to output the heatmap; inference takes the argmax.
Geodesic Target Region Supervision: positives are cells within 1 m geodesic radius of the target (traversability from aggregated depth), all other cells negatives, trained with BCE.

setting.backbone: InternVL2-2B (LoRA fine-tuned) + DINOv2 (frozen) + SECOND-style 3D conv depth encoder + BEVFusion decoder (trained)
setting.training_data: 75K local navigation samples from Landmark-RxR instruction segments rendered in Habitat (70 scenes), with moving pedestrians from Social-MP3D
setting.observation: single-timestep four-view surround RGB-D (448x448, 90° FOV each) plus language instruction
setting.action_space: no low-level actions; outputs an ego-centric BEV affordance heatmap over a ±6.4 m local region, argmax gives a target point
setting.privileged: none at test time (oracle GT maps used only for evaluation metrics; baselines get oracle-view selection)

numbers.extra: trained on 75K samples; metrics averaged over thresholds 0.5/1.0/1.5 m
numbers.evidence: Table 1, Full Validation Set columns, BEACON (Ours)

numbers_note: Custom benchmark built by the authors; no standard nav benchmark results.
results: BEACON achieves 57.72 GeoAcc on the full validation set and 42.83 on the occluded subset, beating RoboRefer-8B-SFT (38.00 / 20.09) by 22.74 points on the occluded subset. SIR drops from 21.49% to 2.60%. It also beats a VLM + MLP point head (41.25 / 32.15).
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation on a self-built dataset; no real-world surround-view RGB-D evaluation
Image-space baselines are evaluated zero-shot with oracle-view selection, not retrained, so the comparison is not fully matched
Failures from landmark/relation confusion and underspecified instructions; single-step prediction without multi-step reasoning or dynamic obstacle avoidance
